mechanism.base: Fire meets fire and neither has to fight the other for air, the old texts say: like lights shine on each other, and like seeks like. One flame set beside another takes nothing from it. Each feeds on what it was given and both grow brighter for the company, until the shared heat outruns what any single hearth can hold. Fire is the one element fed by its own kind and spent by it.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Fire, the flame runs on its own fuel with no second light to borrow warmth from, and the day costs more than it returns. Rest beside someone else's fire once a week.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Fire, the blaze outgrows its hearth and every light nearby reads as a rival for the same air. Warmth meant for company turns to glare. Finish one thing before lighting the next.

function.definition_catalyst: Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Fire makes it warm, so you recover by doing. Running thin, the reserve never builds, and you spend each gain as soon as it comes. You pay for each bright day with a tired one.
function.definition_friction: Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Fire keeps it bright and quick. Running over, your strength wants to carry everything itself, because you count needing others as falling short. You win most days and pay in company.
function.definition_balanced: Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Fire makes it warm, so you recover by doing. In balance, the fire stays lit through a long week. Working alone or racing a friend, you finish with fuel to spare.
function.advise_catalyst: Your strength runs on what you put back, and putting back is the part you skip. Ask one person for help on a job you usually do alone. Get two friends together once a month just for fun. Stand in the sun for ten minutes each morning.
function.advise_friction: Seek Water, the Order energy. Water runs cool and keeps to its banks, and a blaze meets it only on the water's terms. Let it shape what your Fire burns. You take being unstoppable for being well. Hand the lead on one shared job to someone else this month. Hear people out in full before you answer.
function.advise_balanced: Your strength holds while what you put back keeps pace with what you spend. Ask one person for help on a job you usually do alone. Get two friends together once a month just for fun. Stand in the sun for ten minutes each morning.

candidates.cta_verdict: You are your own engine and your own company, so you do your best work beside an equal rather than under anyone's wing.

catalyst.clause: the flame runs on its own fuel with no second light to borrow warmth from
catalyst.remedy: Rest beside someone else's fire once a week.

friction.clause: the blaze outgrows its hearth and every light nearby reads as a rival for the same air
friction.remedy: Finish one thing before lighting the next.

unrooted.clause: No fire of your own under the day: warmth borrowed from whoever stands nearest.
unrooted.remedy: Build one small hearth: a habit that is only yours.

excess.clause: Fire past its task: a blaze that needs ground under it before it has anything left to warm.
excess.remedy: Give it earth: one slow and solid job, finished.

thin.clause: Fire kept low, and rightly: a small flame that lights the day without eating it.
thin.remedy: Keep it small. Feed it only what it asks.

friction.clause: The flame takes the whole table: so much light up close that nothing else at it is visible.

mechanism_yin.catalyst_turn: Run thin, the flame apologizes for shining: warmth dialed down, light waiting to be invited. Your chart asks you to feed the self. Take the seat at the table you keep declining.
mechanism_yin.friction_turn: Run heavy, the flame takes the whole table: so much light up close that nothing else at it is visible, warmth that outshines the people it warms. Dim deliberately sometimes. Leave the far corners dark.

__ore.retired_fn_body: The Core is your endurance function: the seat your strength burns from. With Fire doubled here, your vitality runs on ignition rather than storage: enormous surges, thin reserves, brilliance that outworks anyone for a week and nobody for a season. Bank the coals on purpose. Fuel, sleep, and rhythm are the fire itself, so tend them the way you tend the blaze.
__ore.retired_base_personal: Your core is Fire, and here Fire stands with Fire: flame alongside flame, one blaze sharing a hearth. This is a reinforcement rather than a reaction, the part of your chart that is simply more of you. That is why Fire is your Body: your warmth, your visibility, your refusal to be dim. The other energies act on you. This one is the light itself.

backlog_dips_tg_pattern.mind: You decide by illumination, whole pictures catching at once. Check the flash against daylight.
backlog_dips_tg_pattern.action: Conviction moves you instantly: the moment you see it, you are already lit.

__ore.retired_v3_definition_catalyst:
Fire is your Body, and running thin, it is the energy behind your warmth: sociability, drive, the lift that makes mornings possible. Yours runs in bursts, so depletion shows as dimness with people you love.

Bright in public, flat at home. The laugh still performs, the plans still get made, and the people closest to you get whatever is left, which lately is not much. Warmth on an empty tank comes out as effort.

A light that never recharges becomes an act. Schedule recovery like meetings: real breaks between social blocks, daylight before screens, one morning a week with no one to perform for. Cancel something small today and feel what returns.
__ore.retired_v3_definition_friction:
Fire is your Body, and running over, it is more heat than your days can spend: sleep that will not come, intensity leaking into every conversation, rest that feels like a punishment.

Magnetic, exhausting, on at all hours. The group chat gets voice notes at midnight, small plans become productions, and stillness itches so badly that even holidays get scheduled like campaigns.

Heat needs somewhere honest to go or it goes everywhere. Train to actual sweat most days. Keep one evening a week completely unplanned and endure it. Put the phone down an hour before bed and let the engine actually idle.
